사용자의 손짓, AI의 비평, 사용자의 재감상. 이 과정 전체를 하나의: An iOS interactive artwork encompassing the user's gestures, AI critique, and the user's return to those gestures through reflection.
손짓을 만들고, AI의 비평을 읽고,: Make a gesture. Read the AI's critique.
Return to your own movement with fresh eyes.
The whole encounter is the artwork.
검은 화면에 손짓을 따라 모이고 흩어지는 영문자와 숫자, 기호: Letters, numbers, and symbols gathering and dispersing with gestures against a black screen
Letters to read become material to touch.
It continues when you look again.
나는 손의 움직임을 기록하고, 궤적과 리듬을 AI가 읽을 수 있게 정리했: I recorded hand movements and organized their trajectories and rhythms so an AI could read them. When the AI responds with a written critique, the user sees their own gestures from another perspective. Both making the gestures and interpreting that critique belong to the artwork.
긋고, 멈추고, 되풀이하는 손짓에 궤적과 리듬이 남는다. 사용자는 먼저: Lines, pauses, and repetitions leave traces and rhythms. The user first becomes the artist, making the movement.
화면에서 지나간 움직임은 그 순간의 감각만으로 남기 쉽다. 나는 궤적과: Movement on a screen can disappear into the sensation of the moment. I recorded where and when trajectories, changes in speed, repetitions, and pauses occurred.
평균 속도가 같아도 처음과 끝의 움직임은 다를 수 있다. 숫자 몇 개로: Two gestures can share an average speed yet unfold very differently. Rather than reduce them to a few numbers, I kept their shapes and sequence.
The screens on the right show actual recordings from sessions separate from the visual experience shown here.
파란색과 청록색 선으로 기록된 터치 궤적: Touch trajectories recorded as blue and turquoise lines
기기에 저장된 터치 기록 목록: Touch recordings saved on the device
터치 수와 시간 그래프가 함께 보이는 기록 목록: Recording list showing touch counts and time graphs
AI does not draw for me.
It reads what I have made.
AI에 맡긴 것은 사람의 속마음을 맞히는 일이 아니다. 기록에서 확인할: I did not ask AI to guess the person's inner state. Its critique is limited to forms observable in the recording. It must not assume the maker's emotions or intentions; what the critique means remains for the user to decide.
실제 출력 「A Choreography of Provisional Con: Paraphrased from the actual output, “A Choreography of Provisional Contact.”
AI의 언어는 내가 미처 의식하지 않았던 방향 전환과 반복을 다시 보게: The AI's words offer another perspective on turns and repetitions I may not have noticed. In accepting that critique or reading it differently, the user becomes a viewer again.

Finding new uses for my materials.
Two stories that began with an interface.

with returning to it as a viewer.

Tools I wanted to try, built and refined through use.
A macOS editor for work you can return to.

Drums, melodies, and samples on one timeline.
A workspace for creating, editing, and mixing.
드럼 스텝 시퀀서와 반복 패턴이 배치된 EliteComposer 실제 화: Actual EliteComposer screen with a drum step sequencer and repeating patterns on the timeline
두 작업을 하면서, 인터페이스가 내 행동과 자료를 다시 읽게 만든다는 점: Through these two projects, I kept noticing how an interface could make me read my own actions and materials differently. My gestures returned to me through AI critique, while the order in which I chose PDFs became a record I could use again.
두 앱은 코딩 에이전트와 함께 구현했다. 나는 무엇을 만들지 정하고, 터: I developed both apps with coding agents. I defined what to make and refined how touch was recorded, the limits of critique, the folder views, and the PDF assembly workflow.
드럼·멜로디·샘플을 만들고 타임라인과 믹서로 이어 가는 macOS 음악: EliteComposer is a macOS music-making project connecting drums, melodies, and samples with a timeline and mixer.
Build it into your own track.
Program a rhythm. Add a melody. Mix the sounds.
One workspace connecting creation, arrangement, and mixing.
EliteComposer · Library, Inspector, 타임라인: EliteComposer · Actual workspace with Library, Inspector, timeline, and mixer open
왼쪽 Library와 Inspector, 가운데 트랙 타임라인과 하단 믹: Actual EliteComposer screen with Library and Inspector on the left, the track timeline in the center, and a mixer below
실제 개발 화면 · 화면의 창 제목에는 개발 당시 이름인 Beat Com: Actual development screenshot. The window title uses the earlier name, Beat Composer.
비트를 빠르게 만들고 눈으로 편집할 수 있는 macOS 앱을 만들어 보고: I wanted to build a native macOS app for making beats quickly and editing them visually. As I added a drum sequencer, piano roll, and sample editor, I connected the sounds made in each tool to a shared timeline.
작은 + 버튼에 숨겨져 있던 생성을 ‘New Beat’와 ‘New Mel: Pattern creation was hidden behind a small + button. I brought it forward as New Beat and New Melody. Choose a name, length, and instrument or kit, open the editor, then use Add to Timeline when the pattern is ready.
드럼은 스텝과 세기로, 멜로디는 음높이와 길이로 편집한다. 만든 소스와: Drums are edited as steps and velocities; melodies as pitches and durations. The source you create is separate from where you place it in the track.
드럼 패턴 편집 · 스텝 시퀀서와 반복 클립을 함께 보여 주는 실제 화면: Drum pattern editing · Actual screen showing the step sequencer and repeating clips
16스텝 드럼 패턴과 위쪽 타임라인의 반복 클립: A 16-step drum pattern with repeating clips on the timeline above
스텝과 velocity, 스윙을 조절한다. 기존 패턴을 유지한 채 킷을: Adjust steps, velocity, and swing. Change kits while preserving the pattern, with an explicit option to expand to eight pads.
피아노 롤에서 노트를 그리고 선택한다. 9종 악기와 음색 설정으로 소리를: Draw and select notes in the piano roll. Try nine instruments and sound controls, with settings saved for each pattern.
자르기·반전·페이드·슬라이스 결과를 새 샘플로 만든다. 원본과 기존 클립: Trimming, reversing, fades, and slicing create new samples. The original and its existing clips stay intact.
같은 패턴을 여러 클립에서 참조하게 했다. 패턴을 고치면 반복 리전에도: Multiple clips reference the same pattern. Editing that pattern updates its repeated regions, while each clip keeps its own position and length.
드래그 중 보이는 위치와 실제로 놓이는 위치가 같도록 좌표와 스냅 규칙을: I aligned coordinate and snapping rules so a clip lands where its drag preview shows it. A completed move or adjustment can be reversed with one Undo.
하나의 드럼 패턴을 서로 다른 위치와 길이의 세 클립이 참조하는 배치 구: Concept diagram showing one drum pattern referenced by three clips at different positions and lengths
내용은 같은 패턴을 참조하고,: The clips share the same pattern,
but store their own start, length, and offset.
여러 도구가 타임라인을 밀어내거나 믹서가 편집기 안에 숨어 있으면 작업이: When controls crowded the timeline or the mixer was hidden inside an editor, the workflow broke down. I put the arrangement at the center and gave Library, Inspector, Editor, and Mixer distinct roles.
EliteComposer · 편곡 아래에서 트랙과 출력을 조절하는 믹서: EliteComposer · Actual mixer screen with track and output controls below the arrangement
Drums, Samples와 Stereo Out 채널을 보여 주는 믹서,: Mixer showing Drums, Samples, and Stereo Out channels, with the track timeline above
선택한 리전의 위치와 길이를 Inspector에서 확인한다. 그룹은 함께: Check the selected region's position and length in Inspector. Groups move together, while a double-click opens the source editor for the intended region.
A mixer when you need it.
Editor와 Mixer를 하단에서 전환하고, 닫으면 편곡 공간으로 돌아: Switch between Editor and Mixer in the lower panel, then close it to return to the arrangement. Opening a panel is kept separate from the history of musical edits.
Volume과 pan을 타임라인의 점으로 기록한다. 점 사이의 값을 이어: Record volume and pan as points on the timeline. Values interpolate between points, changing a sound's level and stereo position across the track.
패턴과 샘플, 배치와 작업 공간을 프로젝트에 저장하고, 믹스와 트랙별 스: Save patterns, samples, arrangement, and workspace state in the project, then export a mix or individual track stems. I compared rendered audio before and after saving, and against exports, to check that the work carried beyond the screen.

원본과 편집 값을 구분해 보존하고 레이어·선택·GIF 편집을 연결한 ma: PhotoEditor is a macOS image-editing project that preserves originals and edit settings while connecting layers, selections, and GIF editing.
Keep the original. Keep the work moving.
An image editor connecting layers, selections, and time in one document.
PhotoEditor · 이미지를 불러오기 전의 실제 앱 화면: PhotoEditor · Actual app screen before importing an image
PhotoEditor의 빈 문서. 중앙 투명 캔버스와 이미지 가져오기 안: An empty PhotoEditor document with a transparent canvas and import prompt, tools on the left, and layer and property panels on the right
이미지를 불러오기 전의 실제 앱 화면 · 중앙 캔버스 / 왼쪽 도구 /: Actual app screen before import · Central canvas / Tools on the left / Layers and properties on the right
처음에는 macOS 이미지 편집기를 직접 만들어 보고 싶었다. 레이어와: I started by wanting to build a macOS image editor. As I added effects and GIF editing to layers and brushes, something mattered more than the number of tools: changing tools should not mean starting over.
원본 자산과 조정값을 구분해 보존한다. 레이어와 마스크, 효과를 조합하고: Original assets and adjustment values are preserved separately. Layers, masks, and effects can be combined, then adjusted again.
색이나 객체로 만든 선택을 마스크와 알파 채널로 남긴다. 잠깐 그은 윤곽: Color- and object-based selections can become masks and alpha channels. A temporary outline becomes material for the next edit.
From one image to many frames.
같은 레이어 기반에서 프레임과 시간을 다룬다. 정지 이미지 편집을 GIF: Frames and timing share the same layer-based foundation. Still-image editing connects to GIF playback and export.
이미지를 합쳐 저장하면 조정할 여지가 사라진다. 그래서 편집 가능한 프로: A flattened image leaves little room for revision. I separated the editable project from the image delivered to others. Layers, selections, effects, frames, and referenced assets remain in the project.
새 도구도 같은 문서와 실행 취소 체계를 사용한다. 저장한 프로젝트를 다: New tools share the same document and Undo system. Save a project, reopen it, and continue editing.
원본 자산과 레이어·선택·효과·프레임을 PhotoEditor 문서에 보존: Concept diagram showing original assets, layers, selections, effects, and frames preserved in a PhotoEditor document, saved either as an editable project or an image or GIF
Undo history does not carry over when a saved project is reopened.
이미지를 추가했는데 바로 옮길 수 없거나, 프레임을 놓을 위치가 불분명하: Adding an image without being able to move it immediately, or not knowing where a frame would land, interrupted editing. I described those problems to coding agents, checked the results, and refined the workflow.
새 이미지와 텍스트를 만든 직후 다음 조작으로 자연스럽게 이어지도록 도구: I reviewed tool and session state so creating an image or text could lead naturally into the next action.
Know where the frame will land.
GIF 프레임의 드래그와 재정렬을 다듬고, 타이밍·재생·내보내기를 같은: I refined GIF frame dragging and reordering, checking timing, playback, and export as one workflow.
트랙패드 팬의 방향과 지연을 확인하고, 입력을 모아 처리하는 방식과 렌더: I checked trackpad panning direction and lag, then adjusted how input was coalesced and rendering work reused.
정지 이미지와 GIF를 내보내기 전에 실제 인코딩 결과와 파일 크기를 확: Before exporting a still image or GIF, preview the actual encoded output and its file size. Saving writes those same bytes, keeping the preview and delivered file aligned.
문서 구조부터 비파괴 편집, 선택 도구, GIF와 사용 중 개선까지 담은: A process report covering document structure, non-destructive editing, selection tools, GIFs, and refinements through use. Snapshot: October 19, 2026 · 18 pages · PDF in Korean.

여러 폴더를 함께 펼치고, 같은 원본으로 여러 PDF를 만드는 macOS: A macOS workspace for opening folders side by side and assembling multiple PDFs from shared originals. It preserves your selections and order as well as your files.
Open folders side by side. Assemble the PDFs you choose.
From exploring materials to producing the final files.
실제 앱 화면 · macOS · 개발 중인 작업 공간: Actual app screen · macOS · Workspace in development
폴더를 하나씩 열면 자료의 관계는 사용자의 기억에 맡겨진다. 나는 어느: Opening one folder at a time leaves their relationships in your memory. I wanted to lay out what belonged where on the screen, with several folders open so names and paths could be compared side by side.
폴더 깊이에 따라 항목을 나란히 펼친 병렬 컬럼 화면: Parallel columns showing items side by side at different folder depths
Open several folders together to compare names and hierarchy side by side.
At first, I thought drawing connections would make folder structures easier to understand. But deep folders made the view crowded, and comparing names called for a different layout.
전체 폴더를 볼 때는 그래프를, 파일 이름을 나란히 비교할 때는 컬럼을: Use the graph for the overall structure and columns to compare file names side by side. Both views work with the same files.
한 번 합친 PDF만 남으면, 다음에는 무엇을 골랐는지부터 다시 떠올려야: If all that remains is a merged PDF, the next task starts with remembering what went into it. I saved originals separately from output configurations. The same PDF can belong to several bundles, each with its own order and settings.

원본 PDF와 세 개의 출력, 선택한 출력의 구성 순서가 함께 표시된 실: Actual screen showing original PDFs, three outputs, and the order of items in the selected output
실제 학습 자료를 넣은 화면. 왼쪽에서 PDF를 고르고, 가운데와 오른쪽: Actual course materials in use. Choose PDFs on the left, then configure bundles and order in the center and on the right.
구성 방식을 설명하는 예시: Interactive illustration of the assembly model
오른쪽의 묶음을 바꾸고 자료를 골라 보세요. 원본을 복사하지 않고 각 묶: Switch bundles and choose materials in the example. This web illustration shows how each bundle can reference the same originals without copying them.
원본을 복사하지 않고 여러 출력이 같은 원본을 참조하게 했고, 순서와 설: Multiple outputs reference the same originals, while order and settings are saved separately. The decisions about what belongs together, and in what sequence, can be reopened and continued later.
파일은 한 곳에 있어도, 작업 속 역할은 여러 개일 수 있다. 내가 다루: A file can live in one place and play several roles in your work. I wanted to work with more than a file list: the user's choices and arrangement mattered too.
홀수 페이지 뒤의 빈 쪽, 표지와 뒷표지, 파일명과 쪽번호를 출력 설정으: Output settings include blank pages after odd-page inputs, front and back covers, file names, and page numbers.
다시 찾을 필요 줄이기: Spend less time finding things again.
폴더 탐색에서 고른 자료를 같은 작업 공간의 PDF 구성과 텍스트 편집으: Materials chosen while browsing folders carry into PDF assembly and text editing in the same workspace.
화면 너머의 결과 확인하기: Check the result beyond the screen.
화면의 반응과 실제 파일 작업을 구별하고, 저장과 내보내기의 결과를 확인: I distinguished interface feedback from actual file operations, using saved and exported results as the basis for checking behavior.
